note: Independently rejudged 2026-11-19 against RFC 4271 Section 9.2 and all three current tagged units. The existing route-server positive first establishes useful sole-source output, then requires exactly one withdrawal, no remaining prefix and no duplicate announcement after that source withdraws. The existing negative first proves useful B-then-better-A output, then requires the retained B attributes and zero bare withdrawals after A withdraws. Both inspect ordered recipient TCP history behind a settled-decision barrier and a subsequent wire fence. Their explicit accepting policies, independently installed terminal next-hop routes and real registered bgp-rs, bgp-rib and bgp-adj-rib-in isolate the withdrawal/replacement condition. The two existing route-server discrimination records remain unchanged: queueRecoveryWithdrawal's error-guard mutation omits the owed withdrawal, while Session.recoveryOwedFor returning false bypasses registered source election; the latter is broader than a withdrawal-only cut, and the useful B/A baselines and later exact replacement assertions bound its claim. The additional positive test/plugin/bgp-best-route-transit-default.ci drives actual daemon configuration with internal and forked bgp-rib, explicit grants, accepting export policy and no route-server. Both original sockets complete EOR and next-hop readiness; useful API output precedes a legitimate iBGP UPDATE. The driver verifies the selected source and requires the exact prefix, ORIGIN and two-octet AS_PATH containing local AS 65000 on the original eBGP recipient socket. Native job-advertiser-rfc4271-ordinary-final-record-b523a90d.log records a clean named PASS in 2.2 seconds, followed by the native revert of selectedDispatch.publish and a named broken failure. The internal placement reaches the elected-route socket assertion and receives no announcement; the forked placement loses its deciding process and fails before election can be observed, so this record does not establish a separate forked final-writer failure. The new tag claims initial ordinary IPv4 announcement only. Later withdrawal and API-survivor assertions remain useful controls but add no retirement-specific discrimination or ordinary replacement-present negative claim. Existing route-server claims and records remain separate and supply the no-replacement withdrawal and replacement-present control; the new ordinary positive adds initial advertisement evidence without changing the requirement quote, annotation or existing polarity pair.
